1958 Chevy Apache With Digital 632 Big Block V8 Carries a 'Visceral Z Camaro' to the 2027 SEMA Show
7 photos
Photo: adry53customs / Instagram
The 2026 SEMA Show finished recently in Las Vegas, Nevada, but its echoes linger on, and some folks are already dreaming about the next year’s projects – including the aftermarket realm aided by the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators when they’re not dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI.
For example, Timothy Adry Emmanuel, the virtual artist better known as " adry53customs " on social media, continues his dream ride periplus within the CGI car world and digitally joins the SEMA Show craze. Not long ago, he was on point to provide the renderings for the work-in-progress 1987 Chevrolet Camaro dubbed ‘Visceral Z’ by its builders, Snakepit Customs.
The latter is a custom restoration shop in Clermont, Indiana, and they set out to create the Visceral Z from the 1987 Camaro as a rendering-to-reality project that Adry helped bring to life. They showed it at this year’s SEMA Show even though it’s not complete, and when it’s done, it will have a Wegner Automotive LSX 427 with an 8,000-rpm redline, a Harrop Engineering Hurricane ITB intake, a core ECU by HP Tuners, a Radium Engineering fuel system, PWR Advanced Cooling Technology, Valhalla Fabrication custom-built Tri-Y headers and exhaust, plus a lot more.
Yep, the list continues with a 6XD sequential tucked behind the Roadster Shop FastTrack IRS chassis and will roll on Forgeline AL300s in Carbon Black shod in Hoosier Racing Tire Track Attack Pros, while Wilwood Engineering provided the six-piston front and four-piston brakes. Basically, the pixel master thought it was too rad not to give it a custom companion, and cooked up a virtual 1958 Chevrolet Task Force ‘Apache’ pickup truck for hauling duties.
The latter, together with the Camaro, would be ready for next year’s edition of the SEMA Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, with the Chevrolet sports car being hauled on a custom trailer by this bespoke widebody truck with staggered wheels and a matching paint job, plus a ZZ632/1000 Chevrolet Performance Big Block V8 from GM Performance under the hood.
The pickup truck has restomod touches all over the place, like the LED headlights and rear lights, but it’s built for the track, above all, even in Imagination Land. As such, it comes severely lowered and equipped with an aerodynamic body kit that could make even the extreme folks over at Liberty Walk a bit envious. There are also matching black alloy wheels with the Camaro, and the livery plus the paint emulates it, too.
So, what do you think? Should they start looking for a potential donor truck and start a new build for the 2027 edition of the SEMA Show? Or is it too extreme even for this great trade event?
